A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAVS task and CMR framework. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original segmentation experiments on AVSBench-CI, CIS, and CIM, including component ablations, memory-size experiments, and PVT backbone results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds an open-vocabulary comparison and qualitative failure cases.

M1.justification: CMR retains the same MSS selection criterion, collision-counting algorithm, sigmoid normalization, and 20% memory resampling. Added explanations of sample selection and threshold computation do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same AVSBench-CI, CIS, and CIM coverage. The open-vocabulary comparison uses the existing AVSBench-CI setting. Long-video applicability is discussed in v3 but is not evaluated.

E2.justification: v3 adds Open-vocabulary AVS by Guo et al. (2024a) as an evaluated comparator in Table 7. The original comparator sets, including AVSegFormer and EIR, remain unchanged in the retained experiments.

E3.justification: The added open-vocabulary comparison contrasts frozen inference on novel classes with continued training of CMR, as depicted in Figure 7. The existing incremental splits, disjoint/overlapped settings, mIoU metric, training epochs, and memory budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.6 and Figure 11 add a failure-case analysis concerning visual class confusion and multi-target ambiguity. Existing component, memory-size, and backbone analyses are retained. Section 4.8 largely revisits existing qualitative results and collision statistics rather than adding new measurements.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Collision-frequency statistics are retained method analyses, not new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark, ablation, and PVT values are unchanged. New Table 7 reports base/novel mIoU of 15.9/8.6 for Open-vocabulary AVS and 5.2/35.3 for CMR. The latter differs unexplainedly from CMR's retained 29.5/15.8 in Table 2 under the same stated setting; it does not establish a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: v3 Section 3.2 supplies the missing formal CAVS prediction rule, an argmax over the cumulative label space in Equation 1; v2 introduced this expression without displaying it. The substantive MSS/CSR equations and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged, with no new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: introducing CAVS, identifying two modality-entanglement challenges, proposing MSS and CSR, and demonstrating effectiveness across three incremental datasets.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations addressing visual bias, adaptive thresholds, and sigmoid compression, and interprets the new open-vocabulary comparison. Appendix A.6–A.7 and the conclusion add specific failure conditions and long-video limitations. Earlier interpretations concerning multi-target difficulty and persistent forgetting remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a prospective code-repository link and clarifies baseline adaptation, shared training settings, and per-task unimodal overhead. Its new Section 4.2.1 specifies four NVIDIA 3090 GPUs, while Appendix A.3 retains v2's four L40 48GB GPUs. This introduces conflicting documentation without establishing an actual hardware change.

R1.justification: v3 adds a dedicated multimodal continual-learning subsection and cites Guo et al. (2024a) on open-vocabulary AVS and Li et al. (2026) on visual bias. It removes several 2025 references, including prompt-tuning and recent AVS works, while retaining the central research positioning.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence are retained, with localized explanatory expansions and additional subsections. v3 completes the unfinished abstract ending, adds corresponding-author information, and removes the duplicated appendix heading for collision-class analysis.

P2.justification: The document adopts journal typography and extensively rearranges page layouts and floats. It adds notation and open-vocabulary comparison tables, a comparison diagram, and a failure montage. Previously side-by-side ablation tables become vertically stacked; most original graphical content is preserved.

improvement.justification: Notation clarifications, code-location information, and explicit failure and long-video limitations improve documentation. However, new Table 7 gives unexplained CMR scores inconsistent with the retained main comparison. The added ablation explanation also attributes 25.0 to 27.6 to MSS, although Table 3 gives MSS as 26.5, and hardware descriptions conflict. These additions create reliability problems alongside useful clarifications, preventing a confident net quality judgment.
